statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-65017 (GHSA-c56v-8w4g-3mfm): in a multi-team Apache Airflow 3.3.0 deployment that exposes the Config API, the secrets masker matched only base section and option names, so a team scoped override of a sensitive option, such as a team's Celery broker URL with its credentials, was returned in cleartext to a Viewer with configuration read access. Airflow 3.3.1 fixes it (https://lists.apache.org/thread/kykn94kjf0tntx4wywtvjowh5bzdgf38, https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/70755): the shared configuration parser gains is_sensitive_option, which resolves a team scoped section back to its base section, and the Config API route airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/routes/public/config.py uses it. The advisory affects only Airflow 3.3.0, and no earlier Airflow release was published as this package. We read all 58 airflow packages for Debian 13 published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-17, amd64 and arm64 (116 package files). For every package we read its md5sums manifest, which lists every file the package installs with its digest, and matched the digests of the files that carry the fix against the same files in the released wheels on PyPI; we also unpacked the amd64 and arm64 packages of 3.3.0-0, 3.3.2-19, 3.4.0-0 and 3.4.0-17. Both architectures ship the same copy of those files in every version. 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 install Airflow 3.3.0, 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.1-15 install 3.3.1, 3.3.2-0 to 3.3.2-19 install 3.3.2 and 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-17 install 3.4.0, each with one copy of the file. In 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 routes/public/config.py and airflow/_shared/configuration/parser.py are byte for byte the files in the apache-airflow-core 3.3.0 wheel, and neither has is_sensitive_option. From 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.2-19 both files are byte for byte the apache-airflow-core 3.3.1 wheel's, where the parser defines is_sensitive_option and the route calls it; 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-17 keep the same route file and ship one digest of the parser, and the unpacked 3.4.0-17 parser defines is_sensitive_option. 3.3.1-0 is the first published package with the fix.
